Indian Standard 

METHODS OF CHEMICAL ANALYSIS OF ALUMINO SILICATE 
REFRACTORY MATERIALS 

PART 7 DETERMINATION OF MANGANESE 



1 . Scope — This standard ( Part 7 ) covers a method for determination of manganese ( as MnO ) in 
alumino silicate refractory materials. 

2. Determination of Manganese by Periodate Photometric Method 

2.T Outline of the Method ' — Manganese from a suitable aliquot of the main solution is oxidized to 
permanganate with potassium periodate and measured at 525 nm in spectrophotometer. Amount 
of manganese is evaluated from the calibration curve obtained under similar conditions. 

2.2 Reagents 

2.2.1 Dilute sulphuric acid — 1 : 1 ( vjv ) . 

2.2.2 Concentrated nitric acid— relative density = 1*42 [conforming to IS : 264-1976 
Specification for nitric acid {second revision) ]. 

2.2.3 Phosphoric acid — 10 percent. 

2.2.4 Potassium periodate — Solid. 

2.2.5 Standard manganese solution — ( 1 ml = 1 mg MnO) — Dissolve 0*387 g of pure manganese 
metal in 20 ml hot dilute nitric acid (1:1). Boil out the oxides of nitrogen, cool and dilute to 
volume in a 500-ml volumetric flask. Transfer 25 ml of this solution to 250-ml volumetric flask 
containing 5 ml of concentrated nitric acid and makeup to volume ( 1 ml = 0'10mg MnO ). 

2.3 Procedure 

2.3.1 Transfer a 50 ml aliquot of themain solution [(see2.3.3 of IS : 12107 (Part 2)-1 987 Methods 
of chemical analysis of alumino silicate refractory materials : Part 2 Determination of silica ] to a 
250-ml beaker. Add 10 ml of dilute sulphuric acid. Evaporate to strong fumes on a hot plate and cool. 

2.3.2 Add 20 ml of concentrated nitric acid, 1 mi of phosphoric acid and about 50 ml of water. 
Boil to dissolve the salts and remove nitrous oxides fumes, cool slightly and add 02 g of potassium 
periodate. Transfer to a steam bath to develop the colour and keep for 10 minutes. Cool and 
transfer to a 100-ml volumetric flask, make the volume and mix thoroughly. 

2.3.3 Measure the absorbance at 525 nm against a reagent blank prepared in the same way as 
the test solution without the sample aliquot. 

2.3.4 Calibration curve— Draw calibration curve by taking 0, 2, 5, 10, 15 and 20 ml of aliquots 
of standard solution (1 ml = 0'10 mg MnO ) to six 100-ml volumetric flasks. Proceed in accordance 
with 2.3.2 without the sample aliquot. Measure the absorbance of each solution at 525 nm against 
the reagent blank. Plot the absorbance value against mg of MnO/100-ml of the solution. 

2.4 Calculation — Convert photometric readings of the sample of mg of Mno by means of a 
calibration curve and calculate MnO content as follows: 

A 1 

Manganese ( as MnO ), percent = -=■ x rg 

where 

A — mass in mg of MnO found in 50 ml of aliquot of the final solution, and 
B = mass in g of sample represented by the aliquot taken.

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

Alumino sificete refractory materials contains alumina ( AI2O3 ) and silica (Si0 2 ) in varying 
portions made synthetically by heating aluminium trifluoride at 1 000-1 200°C with silica and water 
vapour. 

It is used in kilns, laddies and furnaces that operate at higher temperature or under conditions 
for which fire clay refrsctories are not suitable. 

This Indian Standard has been prepared in different parts to cover the chemical analysis of 
various constituents in alumino silicate refractory materials. The other parts of the standard are: 

Part 1 Determination of loss on ignition 

Part 2 Determination of silica 

Part 3 Determination of aluminium 

Part 4 Determination of phosphorus 

Part 5 Determination of titanium 

Part 6 Determination of iron 

Part 8 Determination of calcium and magnesium 

Part 9 Determination of sodium and potassium 



Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India
